children: The government has cited the 2018 judgment, which held that parliamentary statements could not override enacted legislation, to clarify its authority to reduce or divest its shareholding in IDBI Bank amid ongoing strategic disinvestment efforts

The Centre has reiterated its legal authority to dilute or divest its shareholding in IDBI Bank, citing a 2018 Delhi High Court judgment that held the government could not be prevented from reducing its stake on the basis of statements made during parliamentary debates.

In a clarification issued on 17 October, the government said an amendment seeking to restrict the dilution of its stake in IDBI was moved during discussions on the Union Budget in 2003 and the parliamentary debate on the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003. However, the amendment was ultimately rejected and did not form part of the enacted legislation.
The government’s statement comes amid media reports and commentary on the legislative developments surrounding its shareholding in the bank.
Delhi High Court ruling on government’s shareholding

The Centre referred to the judgment in All India IDBI Officers’ Association v. Union of India & Others, delivered by the Delhi High Court on 17 December 2018. The court dismissed the writ petition and held that statements made in Parliament during legislative debates could not override the law ultimately enacted.

The court observed that the proposed amendment restricting the government’s ability to dilute its stake had not been included in the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003. It also held that the doctrine of promissory estoppel could not be invoked to prevent the government from reducing its shareholding.
The judgment stated that there was no ambiguity in the Act and no provision that prohibited the government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI.

The doctrine of promissory estoppel generally concerns circumstances in which a promise or representation may be relied upon to prevent a party from going back on it. In this case, the court held that statements made during parliamentary proceedings on legislation could not be treated as a representation that restricted the government’s powers under the enacted law.
Union Budgets signal shift towards strategic disinvestment
The government also cited successive Union Budget speeches to underline the evolution of its policy towards IDBI Bank’s transformation and strategic disinvestment.
In the Union Budget for 2016–17, the then finance minister Arun Jaitley said the government would take forward the transformation of IDBI Bank and consider reducing its stake to below 50%.

The statement, made in paragraph 93 of the Budget speech, formed part of a broader agenda to strengthen public sector banks, operationalise the Bank Board Bureau and outline a roadmap for consolidation.

In the Union Budget for 2021–22, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman listed IDBI Bank among the transactions targeted for completion during the financial year as part of the government’s strategic disinvestment programme. The speech also referred to proposed privatisation initiatives involving other public sector banks and a general insurance company.
Government cites legislative and judicial record

The Centre said the legislative history of the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, the Delhi High Court’s judgment and successive Budget speeches collectively demonstrate the evolution of its policy towards the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank.

It reiterated that the 2018 judgment clarified that parliamentary statements could not be used to restrict the government’s power to dilute its shareholding where the enacted legislation contained no such prohibition.
